name: OmniGraph DB
target_user: Systems Engineers and Data Infrastructure Developers
problem: Traditional graph databases require massive memory overhead and complex external caching tiers to traverse multi-hop relationships without latency spikes under heavy concurrent writes.
pain: Graph traversals hit exponential disk I/O penalties when navigating pointer-chasing patterns across un-indexed property sets.
solution: A zero-dependency property graph database engine written in Java 21 implementing compressed adjacency lists, an explicit property map store, a rule-based query planner, and a custom Cypher-subset parser.
verification: Deterministic integration suite testing graph cycle detection, invalid edge deletion rollback, concurrent multi-hop pathfinding under race conditions, and malformed Cypher syntax throwing explicit parse errors.
major_features: Custom Cypher-subset parser producing an AST for node and edge mutations
Compressed adjacency list storage engine utilizing direct byte buffers
Property map store with type-tagged variable-length attribute encoding
Bidirectional graph traversal engine supporting Breadth-First and Depth-First searches
Rule-based query optimizer generating execution plans from structural statistics
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) for isolated concurrent graph updates
Virtual Thread-based parallel pathfinding worker orchestrator
Crash-recovery engine rebuilding indices from an append-only mutation journal
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
